customManagers.description: Flutter SDK pin across all four workflow files.
flutterpi_tool, activated via dart pub global.
flutter-pi fork tag used by the Pi provisioning script.

packageRules.description: Automerge everything non-major once CI is green.
All non-major pub updates land as one weekly PR.
Action bumps get their own group.

Toolchain and forks are never automerged, at any update type. flutterpi_tool must ship arm64 engine support before the Pi can build a Flutter version, and that has lagged by up to nine weeks — a green desktop CI run proves nothing about it. Bump flutterpi_tool first, then Flutter to whatever it unlocked. 'dart' is the pubspec `environment: sdk:` constraint (datasource dart-version) — the desktop workflow uses `channel: stable` so it would stay green on a raised floor while the Pi's pinned, older Flutter breaks, so it never automerges either. This rule must stay below the broad automerge rule above: Renovate applies packageRules in order and later matches win, so any new automerge rule must be added ABOVE this one, not below. See docs/specs/2026-08-12-dependency-maintenance-process-design.md.

lockFileMaintenance is never automerged, even though it is not a 'major'. It runs weekly regardless — this only stops it from self-merging. A weekly `pub upgrade` can raise pubspec.lock's `sdks: flutter:` floor without touching pubspec.yaml or matching any depName above, so the toolchain carve-out can't catch it: lockFileMaintenance branches have no depName to match. Desktop CI uses `channel: stable` and would stay green on a raised floor while the Pi's pinned, older Flutter breaks. Must stay below both the broad automerge rule and the toolchain carve-out above: Renovate applies packageRules in order and later matches win.

Android Gradle deps and the Gradle wrapper are never automerged. PR CI (build.yml) does not build the APK — only tags, manual runs and the weekly canary do — so a green check proves nothing about them. Run `flutter build apk --debug` before merging.

The Kotlin Gradle plugins (android, jvm, multiplatform, plugin.serialization) and Kotlin libraries move as one PR. Split, each PR conflicts with the last on adjacent lines of android/settings.gradle.kts and main sits on mixed versions in between; the serialization compiler plugin must match the compiler. config:recommended's monorepo grouping did not catch them: 2.4.21 arrived as four separate PRs (#300, #301, …). Must stay below the majors rule so a Kotlin major is grouped too. The regex stops at [.:] so org.jetbrains.kotlinx is not included.
